collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS — NATURE, ECOLOGY AND ANIMALS (NAT-01..50, draft for the owner, 2026-11-15)
Isola's animals, plants, tides and weather: tide pools and nesting beaches, washed-up rubbish, shrinking clam beds, strange visitors, creatures doing what creatures do, and choices about the island where nobody gets a perfect answer.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. Edit anything and send it back; nothing ships until you approve.

collection.description: A swarm of bees has moved into the wall of a villager's hut: coax them into a log hive, or leave them in the wall.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: A swarm of bees has moved into the wall of (subject)'s hut. (subject.He/she) can hear them humming through the thatch at night, and there's already a dribble of honey running down one corner. The bees seem perfectly peaceful. (subject) is less sure about sleeping next to them. (friend), who keeps bees, has come to look.

choices.label: Coax Them Into a Log Hive

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: (friend) brings a hollow log, smoke and a lot of patience. Over two long days, (friend.he/she) moves the comb piece by piece into the log, and the bees follow. (subject) watches from a very safe distance. The log is set up at the edge of the garden. The bees seem to like it. (subject)'s wall is sticky for a month.

o2__fx.name: Outcome B
o2__fx.text: (subject) decides that as long as the bees leave (subject.him/her) alone, (subject.he/she) will leave them alone. The hut hums all summer. Visitors find it unsettling. (subject) finds it oddly soothing, like a song (subject.he/she) can't quite hear the words of. At the end of the season (friend) takes out some of the honey through a gap in the thatch, leaving plenty for the bees. It's the best honey anyone has tasted.
